story_description: Implement smooth animations and transitions throughout the onboarding flow to create a polished, professional first-run experience that feels native to macOS
task_description: Add spring-based animations for welcome logo, page transitions, callout entrances, and toast notifications with full accessibility support for reduced motion preferences
atom_description: Implement the complete animation system for onboarding including welcome logo scale and fade animation (0.8 to 1.0 scale with 1.2s spring), horizontal slide page transitions (0.35s spring), callout entrance animations (scale 0.9 to 1.0 with opacity fade at 0.35s), toast slide-down animations (0.3s ease-out), and comprehensive accessibilityReduceMotion support that disables or reduces all animations when the system preference is enabled
problem_statement: The onboarding flow currently lacks visual polish and animated transitions, making the first-run experience feel static and less engaging compared to native macOS applications that use smooth spring-based animations to guide user attention and provide feedback
scope_in: Welcome logo animation with scale from 0.8 to 1.0 combined with fade-in using 1.2 second spring timing
Horizontal slide page transitions between onboarding steps with 0.35 second spring animation
Callout entrance animations with scale from 0.9 to 1.0 combined with opacity transition at 0.35 seconds
Toast notification slide-down animation with 0.3 second ease-out timing curve
AccessibilityReduceMotion system preference detection and animation disabling
Animation modifier extensions for reusable animation application
Animation timing constants and spring configuration values
scope_out: Toast content or styling beyond animation
assumptions: SwiftUI Animation API provides sufficient control for spring-based animations
The accessibilityReduceMotion environment value is reliably available across macOS versions
Page transition animations can be applied via NavigationStack or custom transition modifiers
Toast views are rendered in an overlay that supports slide animations
Spring animation parameters can be tuned without performance degradation
constraints: All animations must respect accessibilityReduceMotion system preference
Animation durations must not exceed specified timings (1.2s, 0.35s, 0.3s)
Animations must not block user interaction or input
Must use SwiftUI native animation APIs without third-party dependencies
Animation frame rate must maintain 60fps on supported hardware
functional_requirements: Welcome logo displays with combined scale animation from 0.8 to 1.0 and opacity animation from 0.0 to 1.0 over 1.2 seconds using spring timing
Page transitions animate horizontally with slide effect using 0.35 second spring animation when navigating between onboarding steps
Callout views animate on appearance with scale from 0.9 to 1.0 and opacity from 0.0 to 1.0 over 0.35 seconds
Toast notifications animate in from top of screen with slide-down effect over 0.3 seconds using ease-out timing
When accessibilityReduceMotion is enabled all animations either disable completely or reduce to simple opacity fades
Animation state properly resets when views are dismissed and re-presented
nonfunctional_requirements: Animations maintain 60fps frame rate during execution
Animation code is encapsulated in reusable modifiers for consistency
Animation timing values are centralized in constants for easy tuning
Memory allocation during animations stays within acceptable bounds
Animation completion callbacks fire reliably for dependent logic
implementation_steps: Create AnimationConstants struct in Blaze/Sources/UI/Onboarding/AnimationConstants.swift with spring configurations and timing values
Implement WelcomeLogoAnimationModifier view modifier that applies scale and opacity animation with 1.2s spring
Implement PageTransitionModifier that applies horizontal slide with 0.35s spring timing
Implement CalloutEntranceModifier that applies scale and opacity animation with 0.35s timing
Implement ToastSlideModifier that applies slide-down animation with 0.3s ease-out
Create ReducedMotionAwareModifier wrapper that checks accessibilityReduceMotion and applies appropriate animation or fallback
Update WelcomeView to apply WelcomeLogoAnimationModifier to logo image
Update OnboardingNavigationView to apply PageTransitionModifier to step transitions
Update CalloutView to apply CalloutEntranceModifier on appearance
Update ToastView to apply ToastSlideModifier for entrance animation
Add unit tests for animation modifier state and accessibility behavior
Add UI tests to verify animations trigger and complete correctly
ui_states: Logo initial state: scale 0.8 and opacity 0.0
Logo animated state: scale 1.0 and opacity 1.0
Page transition initial state: offset by screen width in transition direction
Page transition animated state: offset 0 at center position
Callout initial state: scale 0.9 and opacity 0.0
Callout animated state: scale 1.0 and opacity 1.0
Toast initial state: offset above screen by toast height
Toast animated state: offset 0 at visible position
Reduced motion state: all elements at final positions with optional simple opacity fade
ui_interactions: User launches app and sees welcome logo animate in automatically
User clicks Continue and sees horizontal slide transition to next page
User focuses a step and sees callout animate in from slight scale-up
Toast appears with slide-down when system message needs display
User with reduced motion enabled sees instant transitions without animation
edge_cases: User rapidly navigates between pages before transition completes
View is dismissed during animation causing potential state inconsistency
Multiple toasts queued while previous toast animation in progress
App enters background during animation execution
System reduced motion preference changes while app is running
Animation triggered on view that is immediately deallocated
failure_modes: Animation fails to start due to invalid spring parameters resulting in static display
AccessibilityReduceMotion value not detected correctly showing animations when disabled
Animation timing exceeds specified duration due to performance issues
Memory leak from retained animation closures causing gradual memory growth
Animation completion handler never called blocking dependent UI updates
rollback_plan: Remove animation modifiers from view hierarchy and delete new modifier files to restore static presentation while keeping view structure intact

na_justifications.api_contracts[0]: Animation modifiers are internal view modifiers with no public API surface exposed to other modules
na_justifications.event_contracts[0]: Animations are visual effects that do not participate in domain event flows
na_justifications.ui_copy[0]: Animation atom focuses on motion timing and does not introduce any new user-facing text strings
na_justifications.test_plan.security[0]: Animation modifiers do not handle user input, credentials, or sensitive data requiring security testing
na_justifications.contracts.apis[0]: Animation modifiers are internal SwiftUI view modifiers with no public API surface
na_justifications.contracts.persistence[0]: Animation state is ephemeral view state not persisted to disk or database

verification_steps: Run xcodebuild test and verify all AnimationModifierTests pass with zero failures
Launch app in Simulator, complete onboarding flow, and visually confirm all four animation types play smoothly
Enable Reduce Motion in System Preferences > Accessibility > Display, relaunch app, and confirm animations are disabled
Open Instruments with Animation Hitches template, run through onboarding, and confirm no frame drops below 60fps
Review PR diff to confirm all six new modifier files are present and applied to target views

risks: Spring animation parameters may feel too bouncy or sluggish on first implementation requiring iteration
AccessibilityReduceMotion environment value may not update in real-time if user changes preference while app running
Rapid navigation between pages could cause animation state corruption or visual glitches
Animation performance may degrade on older Mac hardware with integrated graphics
mitigations: Use Apple recommended spring response and dampingFraction values as starting point then tune based on user feedback
Subscribe to NSWorkspace didChangeAccessibilityDisplayOptionsNotification to detect preference changes at runtime
Implement animation cancellation and state reset when new navigation triggered before previous completes
Test on oldest supported Mac hardware and implement frame rate detection to reduce animation complexity if needed
risk_register.blast_radius: Animation changes are isolated to UI layer modifiers with no impact on data flow, persistence, or business logic. Failure results in static UI only.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If animation issues discovered post-release, ship hotfix that sets all animation durations to zero effectively disabling animations while preserving view structure

events: onboarding_animation_started: emitted when any animation begins with type identifier
onboarding_animation_completed: emitted when animation finishes with duration measurement
onboarding_animation_skipped: emitted when animation bypassed due to reduced motion or interruption
state: AnimationState enum tracks idle, animating, completed states for each animation type
ReducedMotionState boolean derived from Environment accessibilityReduceMotion
TransitionDirection enum tracks forward or backward for page transitions
